title: Anthropic and our route: a proof guide
intro: Choose a step to see what each route does. Labels compare mathematical roles; purple anchors mark exact shared declarations. Green means used only by our selected endpoint, and can include borrowed Anthropic code.
scope_note: These are curated explanations of the existing Lean 4.35 declarations, not new equivalence theorems. The graph, dependencies and positions are unchanged. Our route is the verified implementation variant; the manuscript’s exact algorithm remains separate.

stages.title: 1. Build the piece family
stages.summary: Our construction makes exactly two pieces. Anthropic’s construction makes a parameterized family using partition and operator tables. Both implement the same PiecesF interface.
stages.comparison: Concrete simplification: our piece count is 2 and multiplier is 1; for its chosen partition size h, Anthropic’s count is 4h + 1 and multiplier is h!. This compares the constructions, not their running times.

anchors.name: EthBridge.Elementary.Pieces.family
anchors.label: Our two-piece family
anchors.description: The family fixes cnt = 2, d = 1 and m = 1, and gives explicit bounds for its two program branches.

source.line_text: def family : PiecesF where

anchors.name: ClauseBound.Inst.Half.halfF
anchors.label: Anthropic’s indexed family
anchors.description: The halfF family uses cnt = 4*hF + 1, d = factN(hF), and parameterized partition/operator programs.

source.line_text: def halfF (c₀ c : ℕ) : PiecesF where

anchors.name: ClauseBound.Alg.PiecesF
anchors.label: Shared piece interface
anchors.description: PiecesF describes the programs, piece count, multiplier and size bounds. These two definitions inhabit this exact same interface.

source.line_text: structure PiecesF where

stages.title: 2. Reconstruct the crossing
stages.summary: Our proof groups an existing indexed expansion into low and high parts, then proves that the two collected pieces add back to the crossing. Anthropic’s pieceFacts packages an operator-indexed reconstruction.
stages.comparison: Our identity is A + B = crossing. Anthropic’s sum of indexed pieces reconstructs h! times the crossing. These are different families, not equal corresponding pieces.

anchors.name: EthBridge.Elementary.Crossing.pieceA_add_pieceB
anchors.label: A + B = crossing
anchors.description: pieceA_add_pieceB collects complementary index sets and proves the reconstruction directly.

source.line_text: theorem pieceA_add_pieceB (b : ℕ) (x y u v : Bits b) :

anchors.name: AppHalfPieces.pieceFacts
anchors.label: Indexed reconstruction
anchors.description: The sum field of pieceFacts reconstructs the factorial-scaled crossing as a sum of operator pieces.

source.line_text: theorem pieceFacts : PieceFacts :=

anchors.name: Groundwork.sum_A
anchors.label: Borrowed indexed expansion
anchors.description: Groundwork.sum_A comes from the Anthropic source tree and is invoked in our proof. It is green because only our selected endpoint uses it.

source.line_text: theorem sum_A {n : ℕ} (x y u v : Bits n) : ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), A n i x y u v = cross x y u v := by

stages.title: 3. Meet the same correctness contract
stages.summary: Both families must reconstruct the crossing and supply row/column factorizations with the required bounds. Their correctness proofs target the same PiecesF.Spec interface.
stages.comparison: Our family_spec handles the two cases directly. Anthropic’s stSpec packages its PieceFacts and certified constants for the parameterized family. This is a common contract, not a theorem equating the programs.

anchors.name: EthBridge.Elementary.PiecesSpec.family_spec
anchors.label: Correctness of two cases
anchors.description: family_spec proves the specification for our family; its factorization branches split over the two possible piece indices.

source.line_text: theorem family_spec (h n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) : family.Spec h n := by

anchors.name: GeneralPieces.stSpec
anchors.label: Correctness of indexed pieces
anchors.description: stSpec proves the specification of halfF under the construction’s PieceFacts and constant bounds.

source.line_text: theorem stSpec (hPF : AppHalfPieces.PieceFacts) : StSpec := by

anchors.name: ClauseBound.Alg.PiecesF.Spec
anchors.label: Shared correctness contract
anchors.description: PiecesF.Spec records reconstruction, both cut factorizations and the magnitude/capacity requirements.

source.line_text: structure PiecesF.Spec (P : PiecesF) (h lam : ℕ) : Prop where

stages.title: 4. Certify enough contraction
stages.summary: Both constructions provide the Par certificate needed by the recursion machinery. Our explicit bounds give ρ = 23/24 and c = 2. Anthropic’s partition estimates give ρ = 1/√2 with suitable constants.
stages.comparison: Our contraction certificate is weaker: 23/24 is larger than 1/√2. It is still below 1 and sufficient for this endpoint. The simpler construction does not establish a faster algorithm.

anchors.name: EthBridge.Elementary.PiecesSpec.family_par
anchors.label: Our bound: 23/24
anchors.description: family_par packages our explicit sparse-cut and full-cut estimates into the common parameter contract.

source.line_text: theorem family_par : ClauseBound.Gen.Par family (23/24) 2 := by

anchors.name: ClauseBound.Inst.Half.Par.par_of_cst
anchors.label: Anthropic’s bound: 1/√2
anchors.description: par_of_cst uses certified bounds for the partition-based row and column ranks.

source.line_text: theorem par_of_cst (hS : StSpec) {c₀ c : ℕ} (hC : ∀ lam : ℕ, 1 ≤ lam → Cst c₀ c lam) : ClauseBound.Gen.Par (halfF c₀ c) (1 / Real.sqrt 2) c where

anchors.name: ClauseBound.Gen.Par
anchors.label: Shared parameter contract
anchors.description: ClauseBound.Gen.Par is literally used by both routes; its parameters and family argument differ.

source.line_text: structure Par (P : PiecesF) (ρ : ℝ) (c : ℕ) : Prop where

stages.title: 5. Obtain a counting algorithm
stages.summary: Anthropic’s selected route proves an all-k counting theorem with a minimum of clause-count and variable-count bounds. Our route plugs its family into Anthropic’s existing generic recursion and instantiates k = 3.
stages.comparison: For the ETH goal, we need only the fixed-width counting guarantee. GeneralPieces.partC_n is borrowed Anthropic code but green here: it is reached by our endpoint, not the selected Anthropic endpoint.

anchors.name: CountedRoute.mainTheoremHolds
anchors.label: Anthropic’s full counting result
anchors.description: CountedRoute.mainTheoremHolds supplies the uniform counting theorem used in Anthropic’s route.

source.line_text: theorem mainTheoremHolds : MainTheoremHolds := (closedStatementsFrom onTheCountedRecursion).1

anchors.name: GeneralPieces.partC_n
anchors.label: Borrowed generic recursion
anchors.description: GeneralPieces.partC_n accepts a certified piece family and yields a fixed-width variable-count bound.

source.line_text: theorem partC_n {P : PiecesF} {ρ : ℝ} {c x₀ : ℕ} (hρ : 1 / 2 ≤ ρ) (hρ1 : ρ < 1) (hP : Par P ρ c) (hm : P.m = 1) (hKeeps : P.Keeps) (hx : 18 ≤ x₀)

anchors.label: Our family → counting bound
anchors.description: not_eth_of_pieces supplies the certified family to that generic result at k = 3, then applies the terminal decision conversion.

source.line_text: theorem not_eth_of_pieces {P : ClauseBound.Alg.PiecesF} {ρ : ℝ} {c : ℕ}

exact not_eth_of_countInRateN hα (GeneralPieces.partC_n hρ hρ1 hP hm hKeeps

stages.title: 6. Absorb the machine overhead
stages.summary: Both routes show that the wrapper overhead fits below any positive exponential rate. Anthropic handles its concrete minimum bound and front-end overhead. Our adapter accepts any counting rate r(n) that tends to zero.
stages.comparison: Both invoke the same poly_below lemma. The surrounding lemmas have different hypotheses and bounds; we are comparing their jobs, not claiming they are equivalent.

anchors.name: Wrap.wrapped_time_le
anchors.label: Anthropic’s overhead bound
anchors.description: wrapped_time_le handles the counter’s minimum expression, compact inputs and padding overhead.

source.line_text: theorem wrapped_time_le (q C₁ C₂ a d : ℕ) {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) :

anchors.name: EthBridge.Elementary.DecisionBridge.wrapped_time_below
anchors.label: Our vanishing-rate bound
anchors.description: wrapped_time_below absorbs fixed polynomial overhead around any supplied CountInRateN rate tending to zero.

source.line_text: theorem wrapped_time_below {r : ℕ → ℝ} (hr : Tendsto r atTop (𝓝 0))

anchors.name: Wrap.Arith.poly_below
anchors.label: Shared polynomial bound
anchors.description: Wrap.Arith.poly_below proves that any fixed polynomial fits below a constant times 2^(ε*n), for ε > 0.

source.line_text: theorem poly_below (D : ℕ) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ c : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, ((n : ℝ) + 2) ^ D ≤ (c : ℝ) * (2 : ℝ) ^ (ε * n) := by

stages.title: 7. Turn counting into decision
stages.summary: Both routes wrap an actual counting machine and test whether its count is nonzero. Our adapter needs a subexponential 3-SAT counter; Anthropic’s adapter consumes its compact all-k counting theorem.
stages.comparison: The wrapper theorem is exactly shared. Our proof uses an identity front end for its input format, while Anthropic uses its compact-code/padding front end.

anchors.label: Anthropic’s decision adapter
anchors.description: countingBoundImpliesFailureOfETH consumes Anthropic’s counting guarantee and reaches ETH failure.

anchors.label: Our decision adapter
anchors.description: subexp_of_count_rate turns a supplied 3-SAT counter at any rate r(n) → 0 into a subexponential decision machine.

source.line_text: theorem subexp_of_count_rate {r : ℕ → ℝ} (hr : Tendsto r atTop (𝓝 0))

anchors.name: Wrap.everyMachineCanBeWrapped
anchors.label: The same machine wrapper
anchors.description: Wrap.everyMachineCanBeWrapped is the identical Lean theorem reused by both proofs.

source.line_text: theorem everyMachineCanBeWrapped : EveryMachineCanBeWrapped := everyMachineCanBeWrapped_of coding_exists

stages.title: 8. Reuse the common ETH finish
stages.summary: Both routes derive ETH failure from a subexponential 3-SAT machine, then translate to the common multitape-machine statement. The two marked declarations are literally shared.
stages.comparison: Our route supplies its own counting/decision construction to these conditional bridges. It does not call Anthropic’s old unconditional ETH conclusion.

anchors.description: WidthThree.ethFails_of_subexpTM turns a supplied subexponential 3-SAT decision machine into failure of Sat3.ETH_TM.

source.line_text: theorem ethFails_of_subexpTM (h : Sat3.SubexpTM) : ¬ Sat3.ETH_TM := h.not_ETH_TM

stages.title: 9. Reach exactly the same statement
stages.summary: Both final declarations prove ¬ ComplexityAbstracts.SubexponentialSATAbstract.ETH. The proof terms arrive through different constructions and meet at the same conditional machine-model bridge.
stages.comparison: Our endpoint is the verified two-piece implementation variant with reused recursion. These guide labels do not certify the manuscript’s exact unequal-rectangle algorithm.
